cal roadmap is the global AI leader NVDA ramping Optical connectivity in its next-gen Spectrum-X/Quantum-X AI switches leveraging optical CPO to support its Rubin/Feynman GPUs into 2026. We believe LITE is the leading ultra-high-power InP laser supplier to NVDA SpectrumX/QuantumX switches. We estimate LITE ASP of $50-100/ laser, ~8 lasers per ELS (external laser source), ~18 ELS per Quantum-X switch or 144 lasers per 144 port QuantumX switch, implying ~$11k content per switch. We believe LITE is well positioned as the sole-source supplier for its Spectrum and Quantum switches using CPO, providing a strong first-mover advantage in the space, and growing to ~$517M in F28E, a 416% F25-28E CAGR, with the higher-power CW lasers for CPO driving >50% margins. CPO enables ~50-70% lower power consumption vs current traditional DSP Copper pluggables, while offering higher bandwidth, 3X better reliability, and lower power consumption and we estimate CPO industry adoption reaching 30% by 2030E.

Our  PT$290  is ~33x  F27E  EPS,  above  peers'  25x  P/E driven  by  C26E  EPS  growing  ~87%  y/y above peers' 38% y/y (cons up 84% y/y) and we estimate C27E 33% above peers' 21% y/y and (cons up 25% y/y).

## Risks

Increasing competition from Chinese optical module players with mature supply chains.

Competition from other Optical players Coherent and Broadcom for leading edge AI data center optical solutions in OCS and CPO.

Customer concentration - concentration for DCI with hyperscalers and NVDA with CPO could increase sensitivity in case of an AI spend downturn.

AI demand exposure - the majority of LITE's future growth and share gains are expected to be driven by AI data centers. Any slowdown in expected spending from AI Infrastructure customers could negatively impact LITE's growth prospects.

## Scale OUT with CPO - NVDA Ramping CPO with LITE (Reaching ~13% of F28E Rev from ~0% FY25E)

We estimate NVDA could drive LITE's CPO revenue (via its UHP CW Lasers) growing from ~ $2-4M/qtr today to ~$50M/qtr in JunQ'26, reaching potentially >$500M in F28E. We believe LITE has qualified its UHP 400mw CW Distributed feedback (DFB) lasers at NVDA at potentially ASP of $50-100/pc (7-14x 50mw lasers at ~$7/pc), ~8 400mw UHP CW lasers per ELS (external laser source), ~18 ELS per 144 port Quantum-X SPO switch (16 ELS per 128 port Spectrum-X CPO switch), implying ~$10.8k content per switch ($9.6k per Spectrum-X CPO). The 512x800G port Spectrum X switch could see ~$20k laser content for LITE.
